physics-h2-q2.topic: Connected Bodies Acceleration and Contact Forces
physics-h2-q2.goal: Analyze the underlying scientific principles and deduce the correct conclusion.
physics-h2-q2.material: Object A of mass 3 kg and object B of mass 2 kg are placed in contact on a frictionless horizontal surface, and a horizontal force of 20 N is applied to push on the A side. What are the acceleration of the two objects and the magnitude of the force with which A pushes B, respectively?
physics-h2-q2.thinking.0: Connected Bodies Acceleration and Contact Forces
physics-h2-q2.s.s1.prompt: Object A of mass 3 kg and object B of mass 2 kg are placed in contact on a frictionless horizontal surface, and a horizontal force of 20 N is applied to push on the A side. What are the acceleration of the two objects and the magnitude of the force with which A pushes B, respectively?
physics-h2-q2.s.s1.explain: The overall acceleration is $a = \frac{F}{m_A + m_B} = \frac{20\text{ N}}{5\text{ kg}} = 4\text{ m/s}^2$. The only net force accelerating object B is the contact force with which A pushes B, so $F_{AB} = m_B \cdot a = 2\text{ kg} \times 4\text{ m/s}^2 = 8\text{ N}$.
physics-h2-q2.s.s2.prompt: Which scenario demonstrates the correct real-world application of this principle?
physics-h2-q2.s.s2.explain: The fundamental principles of this inquiry are widely implemented in modern technology.

physics-killer-11.title: The Photoelectric Effect, the Duality of Light, and the Microscopic World
physics-killer-11.topic: The Photoelectric Effect, the Duality of Light, and the Microscopic World
physics-killer-11.goal: Analyze the underlying scientific principles and deduce the correct conclusion.
physics-killer-11.material: Particle P enters a uniform magnetic field $B$ perpendicular to the field and moves in uniform circular motion with an orbit radius of $5\,\mathrm{cm}$ and a period of $2\,\mu\mathrm{s}$. Particle Q enters the same field perpendicular to it, with a mass $4$ times that of P, a charge of magnitude $2$ times that of P, and a speed $3$ times that of P. Ignore gravity. Which option correctly gives, in order, the orbit radius and the period of Q?
physics-killer-11.thinking.0: The Photoelectric Effect, the Duality of Light, and the Microscopic World
physics-killer-11.s.s1.prompt: Particle P enters a uniform magnetic field $B$ perpendicular to the field and moves in uniform circular motion with an orbit radius of $5\,\mathrm{cm}$ and a period of $2\,\mu\mathrm{s}$. Particle Q enters the same field perpendicular to it, with a mass $4$ times that of P, a charge of magnitude $2$ times that of P, and a speed $3$ times that of P. Ignore gravity. Which option correctly gives, in order, the orbit radius and the period of Q?
physics-killer-11.s.s1.explain: Since $r\propto\dfrac{mv}{q}$, $\dfrac{r_Q}{r_P}=\dfrac{4m\cdot3v}{2q}\cdot\dfrac{q}{mv}=6\Rightarrow r_Q=5\times6=30\,\mathrm{cm}$. $T=\dfrac{2\pi m}{qB}$ is independent of speed, so $\dfrac{T_Q}{T_P}=\dfrac{4}{2}=2\Rightarrow T_Q=4\,\mu\mathrm{s}$. Forgetting the charge ratio gives $r=60\,\mathrm{cm}$, $T=8\,\mu\mathrm{s}$ (option 1); assuming the period is proportional to speed gives $12\,\mu\mathrm{s}$ (option 3); ignoring both mass and charge ratios and using only the speed ratio gives $r=15\,\mathrm{cm}$ (option 4).
